claims.finding: MOU proposes a China JV to promote GNEX. Its establishment time and amount remain subject to further discussion. No retail model, ROM, SDK download or shipped game is named.
ICOLS describes the Innocom JV and GNEX/Super GNEX business. The nearby WND dual-concept-phone export announcement does not explicitly establish GNEX on a named WND model.

claims.status: announced development, not a recovered distribution
claims.finding: The article reports a planned first-half-2006 launch, C/C++/Java support and PC/mobile interoperability. It does not supply an installer, binary ABI or device compatibility list. The article URL contains 20060223; displayed publication is February 24.
The incoming Sinjisoft CEO describes plans to commercialize Super GNEX. The 2006 announced deadline must not be treated as proof that a downloadable SDK or retail firmware shipped then.

claims.status: issuer forecast, no retail model proof
claims.source: Issuer PRNewswire release read at ADVFN
claims.finding: Forecast applications include phones, PMPs, DMB devices, MP3 players, laptops and non-mobile displays. The release combines GNEX and a glasses-free 3D LCD module; software VM ABI and display hardware must not be equated. Q3-2007 launch is a forecast.

The filing reports cessation of handset design/solution operations in late 2006, disposal in May 2007, acquisition of a Tsinghua Unisplendour trademark license, and a later assembly-plant plan. Those events do not prove GNEX adoption or termination of the GNEX JV.
